subject: Skyline (rw-skyline) 5xx / timeout surge — customer coordination and recovery
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena@brightbox.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@brightbox.ai; Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RW-Skyline 503 surge observed — immediate impact

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We started seeing a surge of 503s and timeouts against the rw-skyline model on our production namespace around 08:45 PDT. About 20% of our requests are returning 5xx or timing out at 10s, and our downstream pipeline is backpressuring. This started right after a routine increase in query rate tied to a campaign spike.

Can your side confirm whether there is an ongoing degradation with rw-skyline? If so, we need ETA on recovery and any suggested mitigations (model fallback, throttling, or disabling a feature). We also need logs — any guidance will help our SREs triage.

Attaching a short tail of failing requests from our side: skyline-sample-5xx-tail.log

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Moreno
Head of Platform
BrightBox AI

Attachment: skyline-sample-5xx-tail.log (text, 38KB)

Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RW-Skyline 503 surge observed — immediate impact

Thanks for the alert, Elena — we see the same on our telemetry.

Quick summary of what we know now:
- Start time (observed): ~08:42 PDT; scope: rw-skyline model on shared-hosting pool for us-east-1.
- Symptom: elevated 5xx responses and increased tail latencies leading to client timeouts.
- Immediate mitigations in progress: routing fallbacks are being enabled to rw-skyline-lite (compatible variant) for the affected customer namespace, and we are throttling burst concurrency to protect serving nodes.

Actions I'm coordinating now:
1) Marcus (runtime): run a KV cache health pass and check for memory fragmentation / kernel stalls.
2) Rachel (ops): gather GPU and host-level logs; share a concise sample within 30m.
3) Laura (customer success): notify BrightBox about mitigations and estimated next update time.

Elena, can your SREs keep collecting request ids and sample payloads? That will help us correlate. We'll follow up with a detailed timeline and a recommended rollback if necessary.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RW-Skyline 503 surge observed — immediate impact

Short technical update (status at 10:00 PDT):

Observations:
- Reproduced elevated 5xx on canary harness for rw-skyline when a burst of ~6k concurrent short requests arrives (similar pattern to BrightBox traffic).
- Host metrics show progressive GPU memory pressure + intermittent CUDA OOM reclaimed events on three nodes. KV-cache process shows high churn and occasional segfaults in the native cache library (we've captured a core dump).
- rw-skyline-lite fallback serves with ~95% success while slightly increased latency (~30–50ms).

Immediate mitigations performed (10:00–10:10):
- Enabled routing fallback to rw-skyline-lite for BrightBox namespace (traffic shifted, error rate dropped to ~3%).
- Applied temporary concurrency cap on the affected pool to avoid cascading OOMs.
- Restarted KV-cache service on two nodes; collecting heap profiles.

Next steps for recovery and root cause analysis:
- I will forward memprofiling and core dumps to research team; preliminary suspicion is a race in the custom KV cache eviction logic after the new cache-compact patch (deployed 2027-04-30).
- If confirmed, we will roll back that patch for the affected pool and run canary to validate.
- Coordinate a maintenance window for full rollback if required (ETA: 6–12 hours after decision).

Elena — please confirm if continuing with the fallback is acceptable for BrightBox (it preserves correctness but has slightly higher latency).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: skyline-memprofiling-20270504.pdf (60KB)

Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: RW-Skyline 5xx surge — recovery confirmation and postmortem next steps

Hi Elena, Carlos and BrightBox SRE team —

Final update from Redwood: rw-skyline is recovered for your namespace and we are closing the operational incident. Summary and follow-up items below.

Timeline (high level):
- 2027-05-04 08:42 PDT: Increase in 5xx/timeouts observed by BrightBox and Redwood telemetry.
- 2027-05-04 09:00–10:10 PDT: Fallback routing to rw-skyline-lite + concurrency caps applied; error rate reduced from ~20% to ~3%.
- 2027-05-04 10:40 PDT: Identified memory churn and native KV-cache instability correlated with cache-compact patch (2027-04-30).
- 2027-05-04 13:30 PDT: Rolled back cache-compact patch for affected pool and restarted hosts under supervised canary. Errors returned to baseline by 12:40 PDT across the pool.

Root cause (short):
A regression in the KV cache compaction routine introduced in the 2027-04-30 patch caused intermittent native crashes and memory churn under high burst load, which manifested as OOM/reclaimed events on serving hosts and propagated as 5xx/timeouts to customer requests.

What we did for BrightBox (action items completed):
- Enabled rw-skyline-lite fallback during the incident to maintain availability.
- Applied concurrency caps to protect nodes and limit blast radius.
- Rolled back the cache-compact patch for the affected serving pool after validation on canary.
- Ran full host health checks and rebalanced workloads; no data loss.

Planned follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- Marcus: full root-cause write-up and patch repro steps (ETA 2027-05-07 EOD).
- Research: regression test for cache compaction under burst patterns (ETA 2027-05-14).
- CS (Laura): coordinate a short SLO credit for impact window and confirm acceptance (ETA 2027-05-07).
- Ops (Rachel): upload full log bundle and sanitized core dumps to the incident drive link (done).

Attachments and links: postmortem draft and logs have been uploaded — https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Skyline-Incident-Postmortem ; HubSpot reference HS-1029384.

If you would like a walkthrough of the timeline and technical findings, Marcus and I can set up a 30-minute call tomorrow. Again, apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts BrightBox workflows and appreciate your patience.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

--
